findings.title: Keep mesh-scaled roundtrip token IDs inside the vocabulary
findings.description: The mesh-scaled batch makes the fixture legal for CPU8, but scaling arange also scales the token values without bounding them by the fixed 32-row vocabulary. On a legal 32-device mesh the test chooses data=16/model=2 and creates IDs 0..63. The model dimensions remain divisible by this placement (hidden_dim16 over data16, KV heads2 and intermediate_dim24 over model2), so this is not an unsupported configuration. Half the examples then exercise out-of-range embedding indices rather than valid-model roundtrip behavior. Keep batch_size=max(2, data_size), but wrap the generated IDs by model.Vocab.size or tile a valid short token sequence.

# Cold-read result

Commit message: no concrete clarity issues found.

Frozen training-guide excerpt: one ambiguity in the final sentence. It says metadata-less checkpoints require the complete vocabulary from the tokenizer or `override_vocab_size`, while the opening says `override_vocab_size` is applied after restoring the complete checkpoint vocabulary. A first-time reader cannot tell whether, without metadata, that setting must equal the original checkpoint vocabulary size or can still request an export resize. Also, a numeric size supplies a vocabulary size, not the vocabulary itself. Clarify the original-size requirement and whether resizing remains supported in this case.

No source files edited. Review covered only the two requested private payloads.
